source_title: Tottenham v Crystal Palace: Premier League – live
source_excerpt:
Spurs climbed to eighth and left Palace in the drop zone thanks to goals from Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke after Jean-Philippe Mateta’s red card
17h ago Full time! Tottenham 2-0 Crystal Palace
17h ago GOAL! Tottenham 2-0 Crystal Palace (Van Hecke 73')
18h ago Half time: Tottenham 1-0 Crystal Palace
19h ago GOAL! Tottenham 1-0 Crystal Palace (Gray 24')
19h ago Red card! Mateta is sent off for Palace
17h ago Full time! Tottenham 2-0 Crystal Palace
17h ago GOAL! Tottenham 2-0 Crystal Palace (Van Hecke 73')
18h ago Half time: Tottenham 1-0 Crystal Palace
19h ago GOAL! Tottenham 1-0 Crystal Palace (Gray 24')
19h ago Red card! Mateta is sent off for Palace
Here’s Ed Aarons’ verdict from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
The latest Premier League golden boot standings are here; Van Hecke’s second goal of the season means he is now Tottenham’s top scorer this season.
Some post-match thoughts from Jan Paul van Hecke: “We created a lot of chances, the red card helped us … we had to be patient because we know they play a low block. We took a while to score the second, could have scored more, but we’re happy.”
A well-timed Uber Eats ad there, featuring Tony Pulis, Sam Allardyce and Alan Pardew. The ghosts of Palace past!
“I think it was José Mourinho who pooh-poohed the old saw about not looking at the table until 10 games are done; points are points after all,” writes Gary Naylor. “So many clubs seem to be inconsistent or actually imploding before our very eyes. All that manager churn can’t help – coaches need stability to build confidence.”
Save for one nervy moment when Dwight McNeil got a sight of goal, this was very comfortable for Spurs, who took a firm grip of the game after Mateta’s red card. There will be tougher tests ahead, but Tottenham look like a cohesive team again. Palace, on the other hand, look to be in trouble.
92 mins: Kulusevski unleashes a rocket towards the top corner, but Henderson is equal to it again. He’s been Palace’s best player.
90 mins: A lovely little cameo from Williams-Barnett, jinking through Palace defenders like a spring lamb and squaring for Kudus – who shanks away from an open goal in the Sunday League style.
88 mins: Sage hooks Wharton and Kamada, throwing on Will Hughes and Jefferson Lerma. “It’s been Van Hecke of a game for Spurs!” honks Peter Oh.
87 mins: Tel takes his leave after a very impressive display, and he’s replaced by homegrown hopeful Luca Williams-Barnett. Big cheers all round.
85 mins: Kudus gets in behind the back four and flicks the ball past Henderson – but he looks a mile offside, and the flag duly goes up.
83 mins: Not much happening now, as Palace fans contemplate that long cross-capital journey home. On which subject, here’s Julian Borrill: “Just looking at London, the longest trip looks like Bromley to Wealdstone at 1hr 54min. But a shout-out to Brentford-Hornchurch at 1hr 24min – all on the District Line.”
81 mins: Another fine stop from Henderson, springing to his left to save Gallagher’s goalbound shot. Palace look like they’re going to need him if they’re to stay out of trouble.
79 mins: Should they hold on to this lead, Tottenham will move up to eighth. Their next four games are Leeds (A), Ipswich (H), Sunderland (A) and Fulham (H) – and then it’s the North London Derby.
76 mins: Kulusevski and Udogie come on, replacing Marmoush and Robertson. Now their injury problems are easing, Spurs’ bench is starting to look quite stacked.
The centre-back has been playing almost as an auxiliary forward in the second half, and he does a decent Harry Kane impression here, stretching to beat two Palace defenders with a header. Henderson saves, it hits the underside of the bar, then bounces in off Van Hecke’s bonce as he falls to the floor.
Spurs finally have their second goal, thanks to Jan Paul van Hecke, who bundles home Fernandes’ superb cross at the far post. Game over now, surely.
71 mins: Oof! Robertson plays an instinctive one-two with Marmoush, but his touch then lets him down and he’s forced to try and chip Henderson from an impossible angle, sending the ball behind.
69 mins: A potential Palace breakaway is halted by a handball decision. Still, with 20 minutes to go, the visitors have a route to get a result, which looked unlikely at half-time.
67 mins: Tel tries to recreate his clinical finish at Stamford Bridge, but sends his shot crashing into the hoardings to the left of goal.
65 mins: Pedro Porro is the latest Spurs player to fire high and wide. A second change from De Zerbi: Conor Gallagher is on, replacing Solanke and allowing Marmoush to push further forward.
63 mins: Marmoush has options to his right, but his pass is poor and cut out by Mitchell – only to then ricochet back towards Henderson, who has to parry it away! Proper pinball stuff at either end.
62 mins: Maybe now, as Kamada’s cross floats across the Spurs box and finds McNeil’s boot – but his well-struck shot is blocked by Solanke. That gives Tottenham the chance to break …
61 mins: Van Hecke has a blast from 30 yards out that isn’t particularly close. At what point do Spurs fans start to get antsy about this slender lead?
59 mins: Two changes for Palace, with Anan Khalaili and midweek scorer Eddie Nketiah replacing Pino and Mingueza. Spurs fans give former Gunner Nketiah a frosty reception.
58 mins: Pino is robbed in midfield and Spurs use the little bit of extra space, Tel finding Solanke whose shot is deflected behind. A tenth corner for the hosts, but it comes to nothing.
56 mins: Jan-Paul van Hecke finds himself in the area and has a shot that’s charged down at close range. Pierre Sage, who sounds to me like a French philosopher, chews on his pipe and ponders some changes.
54 mins: In the first 10 minutes of the second half, the ball has spent about 20 seconds in the Spurs final third. There’s a penalty shout as Fernandes’ shot hits Disasi on the shoulder, but not low enough to interest the VAR.
53 mins: Mingueza goes in the book after catching Tel with a flailing arm. From the free kick, Spurs keep the ball and keep the pressure on.
52 mins: Possession is close to 80-20 in Tottenham’s favour, and the territorial battle must be even more one-sided. The hosts’ latest attack ends when Solanke is penalised for a foul.
50 mins: Solanke is next to have a go, taking down Perro’s cross, swivelling and lashing a shot at goal. It’s central, but Henderson still has to throw up a strong arm to stop the power alone beating him.
49 mins: Robertson and Tel are working well together on the left, and the full-back curls in a cross that Marmoush can only head towards Henderson.
46 mins: Tel’s shot is deflected off Richards’ shins for a corner, which is headed out into the path of Fernandes. He drills a shot that is flicked off target by a Palace boot – I think that was heading in.
A half-time change for Spurs, with Pedro Porro replacing the goalscorer, Archie Gray. Not sure if that’s injury-related – Gray was excellent in the first half.
“Re: Mateta. If a player decides to slide in, uncontrolled from behind, with their studs up … c’mon, we’ve all got work in the morning,” writes David Penney.
Spurs end the first half a goal and a man up thanks to Archie Gray’s header, after Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off following a VAR review. The hosts have dominated, but need another goal or two to avoid any second-half nerves.
46 mins: Unfortunately, Dwight McNeil’s through ball lands harmlessly in the giant, Jean-Philippe Mateta-shaped hole in the Tottenham half.
45 mins: Two added minutes, and another Spurs free kick to fend off for Palace. Fernandes’ cross is cleared at the far post, and Palace try to break …

## टोटेनहम की प्रिमियर लीग में महत्वपूर्ण जीत

प्रिमियर लीग के एक मुकाबले में टोटेनहम हॉटस्पर ने क्रिस्टल पैलेस को 2-0 से हरा दिया है। इस जीत के साथ टोटेनहम अंक तालिका में आठवें स्थान पर पहुंच गई है, जबकि क्रिस्टल पैलेस की टीम तालिका के निचले हिस्से में संघर्ष कर रही है।

## मैच के मुख्य आकर्षण

* **पहला गोल:** मैच के पहले हाफ में आर्ची ग्रे ने शानदार हेडर के जरिए टोटेनहम का खाता खोला और टीम को बढ़त दिलाई।
* **लाल कार्ड:** क्रिस्टल पैलेस के ज्यां-फिलिप मतेटा को वीएआर (VAR) समीक्षा के बाद फाउल के चलते लाल कार्ड दिखाकर मैदान से बाहर भेज दिया गया।
* **दूसरा गोल:** मैच के 73वें मिनट में जान पॉल वान हेक ने दूसरा गोल कर टोटेनहम की बढ़त को मजबूत किया। इस सीज़न में उनका यह दूसरा गोल है।

## मैच की स्थिति और आगे के मुकाबले

मैच के अधिकांश समय में टोटेनहम का पलड़ा भारी रहा और उन्होंने गेंद पर अपनी पकड़ बनाए रखी। क्रिस्टल पैलेस के गोलकीपर ने कुछ बेहतरीन बचाव जरूर किए, लेकिन उनकी टीम एक खिलाड़ी कम होने के कारण वापसी करने में असमर्थ रही।

मैच के बाद खिलाड़ियों ने अपनी प्रतिक्रिया देते हुए कहा कि शुरुआती बढ़त और लाल कार्ड मिलने से उन्हें खेल को नियंत्रित करने में मदद मिली। टोटेनहम का अगला सामना आगामी मुकाबलों में होगा, जबकि क्रिस्टल पैलेस को अपनी स्थिति सुधारने के लिए अगले मैचों में बेहतर प्रदर्शन करना होगा।

*मूल घोषणा और विस्तृत जानकारी के लिए आधिकारिक प्रिमियर लीग प्रसारण और संबंधित खेल पोर्टल्स की सहायता ली जा सकती है।*

en_body:
## Match Summary

Tottenham claimed a 2-0 home victory against Crystal Palace in the Premier League, moving up to eighth place in the league table while leaving Crystal Palace in the relegation zone. The match turned decisively in the first half when Palace forward Jean-Philippe Mateta received a red card following a VAR review.

* **First-half breakthrough:** Archie Gray opened the scoring for Tottenham in the 24th minute with a header.
* **Securing the points:** Jan Paul van Hecke added Tottenham's second goal in the 73rd minute, bundling home a cross at the far post after it hit the underside of the crossbar.
* **Palace struggles:** Playing with ten men for a significant portion of the match, Crystal Palace relied heavily on goalkeeper Dean Henderson, who made several key saves to keep the scoreline down.

## Post-Match Perspectives

Speaking after the game, Tottenham goalscorer Jan Paul van Hecke noted that his side created numerous chances and that the red card aided their control of the match, though acknowledged that the team needed to be patient against Palace's low block defensive setup. 

With the result, Tottenham's upcoming league fixtures feature matches against Leeds, Ipswich, Sunderland, and Fulham before the North London Derby. Meanwhile, Crystal Palace faces mounting pressure at the bottom end of the standings as they look to steer clear of the drop zone.

## How to Verify

Readers can check official Premier League standings, club websites for Tottenham Hotspur and Crystal Palace, or recognized sports broadcast networks for complete match statistics, line-ups, and subsequent fixture updates.
